properties.areaDesc: Lower Kobuk Valley; Baldwin Peninsula
properties.headline: Blizzard Warning issued October 22 at 8:41PM AKDT until October 24 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions expected. Total snow accumulations
between 1 and 3 inches. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Baldwin Peninsula and Lower Kobuk Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility. Visibilities may drop below
a quarter mile due to falling and blowing snow. Very strong winds
could result in power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow and gusty winds will produce blizzard
conditions Friday. As south winds continue and temperatures warm,
snow will transition to rain potentially as early as Friday
evening. Strongest wind gusts will be Friday afternoon into early
Saturday morning.
properties.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. If you must travel,
have a winter survival kit with you. If you get stranded, stay with
your vehicle.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Broward County; Coastal Miami Dade County
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 23 at 12:36AM EDT until October 24 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT
Saturday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT
Saturday. The advisory will either need to be extended into
next week or upgraded to a warning Sunday into Monday when
King Tides peak and rain chances and onshore winds are
highest. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Montezuma, CO; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 10:35PM MDT until October 23 at 12:45AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...West Central Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southeastern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1245 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1032 PM MDT, Flooding is ongoing in the warned area. Between
1.2 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes, but is not limited to, the following streamsand
drainages...
Florida River, Spring Creek, Ute Creek, Salt Creek and Dry Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Low-lying areas along McElmo Creek between Cortez and Aneth.
- Flooding is ongoing at Bartlett Wash and Hunters Canyon.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

crossings may be flooded.

over the region through the predawn hours before tapering off
around sunrise. Additional rain amounts for the rest of tonight

amounts up to 1.50 inches.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

to take action should flooding develop.

FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Catron County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 200 AM MDT.

* At 957 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1.25 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Gila Cliff Dwellings and Beaverhead.
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Grant County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 1230 AM MDT.

* At 929 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
San Lorenzo, Hurley, Cobre, Bayard, Mimbres, Hanover, North Hurley,
Santa Clara, Shingle Canyon, Bear Canyon, Allie Canyon and Soldiers
Canyon.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 23 at 12:32PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 97W continues to develop over the northern Marshall Islands,
centered near 11N166E in the vicinity of Bikini and Rongelap Atolls.
97W is now the subject of a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA)
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), meaning it is expected
to develop into a significant tropical cyclone (a tropical
depression) within 24 hours. Himawari visible satellite imagery this
afternoon shows numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms across
the northern Marshall Islands, focused mainly over the
northwesternmost islands and atolls. Scatterometry data from this
morning shows fresh to strong west winds near Ujae and Ebadon Atolls,
and surface observations on Kwajalein Island are showing fresh west
winds with frequent strong gusts. Near-gale force gusts have been
observed with passing showers, and significant boat damage was
recently reported along west-facing exposures of Kwajalein as well.

Surging west winds are expected to continue across the western and
central Marshall Islands, south of Invest 97W's center, and boats
should be safely moved from west-facing exposures and secured, if
possible. Fresh to strong west winds will begin to shift
southwesterly tonight as 97W strengthens, and persist through Sunday
as 97W begins to lift north out of the RMI. Locally heavy showers
will be possible across the northern half of the Marshall Islands
through the weekend. Showers and winds will begin to diminish Sunday
night as 97W pulls farther away, but elevated west to southwest swell
associated with the disturbance may persist into early next week.
Elevated surf along west and south reefs may become hazardous this
weekend into early next week as these swells persist. This situation
will be closely monitored for additional impacts to the Marshall
Islands.

For more information on Invest 97W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

NWSheadline: INVEST 97W DEVELOPING OVER THE NORTHERN MARSHALL ISLANDS, NOW THE SUBJECT OF A TROPICAL CYCLONE FORMATION ALERT... ...LOCALLY HEAVY SHOWERS, SURGING WEST WINDS AND SWELL EXPECTED

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 22 at 9:44PM AST until October 23 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the HIGH SURF ADVISORY, large breaking waves of 8 to
12 feet. For the HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, life-threatening rip
currents.

* WHERE...For the HIGH SURF ADVISORY, the most vulnerable areas
for high surf and beach erosion include Pinones along Road
187, Parcelas Suarez, Villas del Mar, and Villa Christiana in
Loiza; Fortuna in Luquillo; Pueblo and Tamarindo in Aguadilla;
Barrio Obrero, Pueblo and Jarealito in Arecibo; La Boca in
Barceloneta; Machuca in Manati; Puerto Nuevo in Vega Baja;
Ocean Park in San Juan; and Barrio Espinal in Aguada. For the
HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, beaches along the west to northeast
coast of Puerto Rico.

* WHEN...For the HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK through Saturday afternoon.
For the HIGH SURF ADVISORY from 6 AM to 6 PM AST Friday.

* IMPACTS...FOR THE HIGH SURF ADVISORY, High waves that can wash
over jetties and sweep people and pets onto jagged rocks.
Rough surf may also knock you down. Large breaking waves will
result in localized beach/dune structure erosion and dangerous
swimming conditions. FOR THE HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

Creek, Pumphouse Wash and Verde River.

- For Oak Creek at Oak Creek at Sedona:

Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 8.04 feet is expected at 7:00pm Thursday.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sedona, Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs, Indian Gardens, Pine
Flats, Uptown Sedona, Red Rock State Park, Slide Rock State Park,
West Fork of Oak Creek, Red Rock-Secret Mountain Wilderness,
Cathedral Rock, East Pocket Lookout Tower and Oak Creek Vista
Overlook.
- This includes the following highways...
State Route 179 between mile markers 310 and 313. State Route 89A
between mile markers 374 and 393.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Manzanita Campground, Pine Flat Campground, Cave Springs
Campground and Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Pumphouse Wash, Slide Rock, Encinoso, Grasshopper Point, Midgely
Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing", Crescent Moon Ranch and
Mormons Crossing.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 9:03PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the weekend. There
is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage next week,
after northeast winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Thursday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

and Gobernador Canyon near Blanco and Archuleta.

properties.areaDesc: Hatteras Island
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 22 at 8:09PM EDT until October 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous
rip currents and large breaking waves expected in the surf
zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT Friday through
Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Ocean overwash impacts expected to gradually improve
as waves subside overnight and Friday. NC-12 between the
Basnight Bridge and Rodanthe remains closed. The next high tide
is around 545 AM Friday. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore
break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom
causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around noon Friday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

properties.areaDesc: Hatteras Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 8:09PM EDT until October 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous
rip currents and large breaking waves expected in the surf
zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT Friday through
Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Ocean overwash impacts expected to gradually improve
as waves subside overnight and Friday. NC-12 between the
Basnight Bridge and Rodanthe remains closed. The next high tide
is around 545 AM Friday. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore
break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom
causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around noon Friday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 22 at 3:54PM AKDT until October 24 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 35 to 50 mph with gusts up to 75
mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, Platinum and Goodnews Bay, and Northern
Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Friday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are expected to start by 1
PM AKDT Friday for the Kuskokwim Delta, Northern Bristol Bay,
Platinum, and Goodnews Bay. For the Western Capes, the strongest
winds are expected near Cape Newenham, with winds for Platinum and
Goodnews Bay expected to be near 60 mph. For Northern Bristol Bay,
the strongest winds are expected near Togiak, while gusts up to 50
mph are expected for Dillingham. Winds are expected to steadily
diminish through Saturday as the front moves inland and weakens.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must drive.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 5:44PM MDT until October 23 at 5:45AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 545 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Several structures are
flooded, and numerous roads remain closed due to flooding impacts
County wide. Streams will likely continue to rise due to excess
runoff and additional rainfall expected overnight.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 528 PM MDT, Public and local law enforcement reported numerous
impacts of flooding occurring across Archuleta County. Between
1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area this evening and overnight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pagosa Springs, Lonetree, Chimney Rock, Juanita, Gato, Pagosa
Junction, Chromo and Arboles.
- The San Juan River continues to rise, and is expected to exceed
Major Flood Stage late this evening and overnight. This flood
warning extends to tributaries, streams, creeks and low-land
areas beyond the San Juan River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 3:43PM AKDT until October 24 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 2.0 to 3.0 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 35 to 50 mph winds with
gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...8 AM Friday through 1 AM Saturday, particularly around
high tides near 10 AM and 10 PM Friday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely scenario is for water
levels to be 2.0 to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide line.
While unlikely, the worst case scenario for Kipnuk is for water
levels to be 3.5 to 4.0 feet above the normal high tide line,
while the worst case for Kwigillingok is 4.0 to 5.0 feet above
the normal high tide line. The 10 PM Friday peak, with the
aforementioned high tide, is expected to be the higher of the
two peaks. We are closely monitoring this storm. In the
meantime, please have a plan in place.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Bristol Bay Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 22 at 3:43PM AKDT until October 24 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels most likely around 1.0 to 2.0 feet above
the normal highest tide line, with highest water levels
expected near Togiak.

* WHERE...Northern Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...10 AM Friday to 7AM Saturday

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Bering front arrives to the Southwest
Alaska coast Friday morning, bringing a prolonged period of
strong southerly winds towards the coast. These winds will
result in elevated water levels and high surf. This period of
winds will coincide with two tidal cycles and push water
levels 1.0 to 2.0 feet above the normal highest tide line.
Water levels are expected to quickly drop off Saturday morning
as winds decrease, alleviating coastal concerns.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 7:17PM EDT until October 24 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler and Southeast Coastal
St. Johns Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Saturday
night. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT
Saturday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Friday night
through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 22 at 3:08PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
The following statement was issued by the Oklahoma Department of
Environmental Quality until 10 PM CDT Saturday evening.

An Air Quality Alert for Ozone has been issued for Friday, October
23rd for the Oklahoma City Metropolitan area due to expected high
concentrations of ozone.

Public Health Recommendations: Persons with existing heart or
respiratory ailments should reduce physical exertion and outdoor
activity.

The general public is encouraged to help alleviate the problem by
reducing vehicle miles traveled by riding the bus, carpooling, or
avoiding unnecessary trips. The public is also asked to avoid
refueling during the morning and early afternoon hours, and to avoid
the use of two cycle engines such as lawn mowers, motorcycles, weed
trimmers, and outboard engines. It is also advised to limit outdoor
burning.

To view the latest air quality map, visit airnow.gov or the AirNow
app.

For hourly updates on concentrations and possible health warnings,
telephone the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality at
405-702-4100. For more information on health effects, call the
American Lung Association of Oklahoma at 405-748-4674

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is occurring.
Prolonged and widespread moderate to heavy rainfall will continue
trough this evening. This coupled with near-saturated soils will
allow flows to remain high across all waterways within the warned
area, including all of the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area.
High flows are expected to continue within, but not limited to...
the Paria River, Wahweep Creek, Warm Creek, Last Chance Creek,
Croton Canyon, and the Escalante River Basin and tributaries. Many
backcountry roads within this area are expected to become
impassable.

- At 1154 AM MDT, Widespread flooding is already occurring in the
warned area. A recent example is the Escalante River near
Escalante reaching a new high flow for this event of 1660 cfs
over the last hour. After reaching a peak of 2500 cfs on the
Paria River last evening, flows have decreased but continue to
run high and swift, and additional rises remain likely. Between 1
and 3.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

unstable and unsafe.

properties.areaDesc: Imperial County Southwest; Imperial County West; Imperial Valley
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 22 at 7:36AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...the Imperial Valley. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Thursday, October 22, 2026 until 11:00 PM.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...The beaches of Volusia, Brevard, Indian River, Saint
Lucie, and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 21 at 5:53AM MST until October 22 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An upper-level trough will bring a deep surge of subtropical and
tropical moisture into our region. Showers and thunderstorms will
develop across much of northern and central Arizona early
Wednesday morning and continue through Thursday evening. Stronger
